title: Correct initial gas volume
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the initial gas volume in the bottle as the bottle volume minus the liquid volume (0.9 mL - 0.5 mL = 0.4 mL).

title: Apply Boyle's Law (first injection)
description: Important: Student applies Boyle's Law (pV = constant) to the isothermal mixing of the initial bottle gas and the first syringe gas, using the correct combined initial volume.

title: Final pressure after first injection
description: Essential: Student provides the correct final pressure for part (1): 1.1 × 10^5 Pa.

title: Apply Boyle's Law (second injection)
description: Important: Student correctly models the second injection by applying Boyle's Law to the gas already in the bottle (at pressure p1) mixing with a new syringe volume at atmospheric pressure.

title: Final pressure after second injection
description: Essential: Student provides the correct final pressure for part (2): 1.2 × 10^5 Pa.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student demonstrates consistent use of volume units (mL or cm³) and pressure units (Pa) throughout the calculation.

title: Misapplication of gas laws
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly assumes pressures add directly or misapplies the ideal gas law by not accounting for volume changes during gas transfer.

title: Incorrect initial state
description: Pitfall: Student uses the full bottle volume (0.9 mL) instead of the gas volume (0.4 mL) as the initial volume for Boyle's Law.
